chunks: As for what al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an owned slave who slanders a free man. He said: “He is lashed eighty times. This is from the rights of the Muslims. As for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then he is struck with half of the hadd.” I said: What is that which is from the rights of Allah? He said: “If he commits zina or drinks wine, then this is among the rights in which half of the hadd is administered.”

So this is an anomalous report, by which the mutawatir reports concerning the inclusion of the wine-drinker and his deserving eighty lashes are not opposed. Those reports are general regarding slaves and free persons, and we have also narrated what specifically includes them in wording as well, and their deserving the complete hadd; therefore, it is not appropriate to object to all of them with this report. It is possible that the narrator heard that only concerning zina in particular, because it is from the rights of Allah, and since the hadd of the wine-drinker is from the rights of Allah, he applied it to that; but it is not proper for us to apply it thus, because it is not impossible that the fornicator among them be specified with half of the hadd, while the wine-drinker is given the hadd in full, even though both are from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then it is also possible that the explanation in it is what we mentioned in the first report, namely taqiyyah, due to its accordance with the doctrines of some of the ʿAmmah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: rights belonging to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the legal sense
key_terms.حُقُوقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: rights belonging to human beings that are legally owed to them
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report that stands apart from stronger transmissions
key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused or slandered someone with fornication
key_terms.نِصْفَ الْحَدِّ: half of the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Does a slave receive half or the full hadd punishment for drinking wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses hadd punishments for a slave, distinguishing between the rights of people and the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The accompanying scholarly note states that the report is anomalous regarding drinking wine, since more widely transmitted reports establish eighty lashes for the wine-drinker, and it suggests either a restriction to zina or an interpretation based on taqiyyah.
